Auto-generated Summary (brief):
LynxPath is a regional reseller and managed GPU provider looking to evaluate Redwood as an inference runtime partner to offer bundled Dedicated/Private deployment options to their enterprise customers. Key concerns: compatibility with LynxPath's multi-tenant scheduler, VPC peering and SAML SSO, KMS/HSM integration, and margin + pricing for reseller SKUs. Next: pilot bench for quantized model, share runbook/security pack, pricing draft.

Topics Covered:
- Reseller program mechanics and margins
- Private (VPC) deployment and network connectivity
- On-prem / hybrid GPU compatibility and quantization testing
- Security: SOC 2, SSO, KMS, audit logs
- Pilot scope: workload, RPS, SLA targets

\Transcript (timestamps approx every ~30s):
[00:00] Ethan Patel: hey everyone, thanks for making time, um i'm Ethan from Redwood, i'll kick us off. we got Priya our SE and Liam from solutions, and then from LynxPath?
[00:05] Roberto Silva: hey Ethan, yep this is Roberto, thanks for the invite. we wanted to run through how Redwood might fit into our reseller stack, basically can we host a private offering for our customers and route through our billing etc.
[00:12] Priya Nair: cool, hi hi. quick agenda: intro, high-level product fit (hosted vs dedicated vs private), security & networking, pilot framing, Q&A. sound good?
[00:20] Asha Menon: yep that's perfect. we have some integration folks on the call, David's here to go into cluster details.
[00:25] David Kim: hey all. quick aside — our infra is a mix of on-prem racks and co-lo A100s with a custom scheduler, multi-tenant nets. we want to avoid forcing customers to re-architect.
[00:33] Ethan Patel: totally makes sense, the usual pattern we see is either Redwood Dedicated where you reserve pools and we manage the runtime but it's isolated for you, or Redwood Private which ships a control plane in your VPC so you keep networking and keys. both are compatible with an overlay scheduler but there are some integration points.
[00:48] [crosstalk] Roberto Silva: so let me stop you — what does the control plane actually need? like peering, ports, VPN? is that a lot of work?
[00:55] Priya Nair: short answer — VPC peering or Transit Gateway is typical, we need outbound API reachability to our control plane if you choose hosted control plane, or we can do a customer-managed control plane that talks to your internal services. ports are minimal, TLS over 443, and we have an agent for metrics and tracing.
[01:10] Maya Ortiz: procurement question — for reseller deals do you provide net 30 terms or how does that usually work on pilot?
[01:16] Ethan Patel: for pilots, usually upfront credit or invoice, net terms are possible at enterprise contract stage; we'll put pricing tiers for reseller SKUs in the doc we send.
[01:24] David Kim: on the compute side we run mixed precision workloads and plan to test int8 quantized models. how does Redwood handle quantized execution and token-level batching?
[01:31] Priya Nair: our runtime supports quantized kernels and has a batching layer that aggregates requests while preserving latency SLOs; when you run int8 model variants we can suggest kernel settings and batch sizes — the tradeoff is throughput vs latency and we have heuristics. sometimes the scheduler needs minor tuning to avoid token cache evictions.
[01:47] Roberto Silva: minor tuning — can you be more concrete? because our scheduler does preemption and dynamic slotting. preempt causes KV cache resyncs which are expensive for long-chat sessions.
[01:55] Priya Nair: yep we face that. options: sticky sessions to keep KV caches pinned to GPUs for active sessions; or we can recommend longer-lived slots for chat-like workloads. alternatively, enable prefix caching on the control plane so we can rehydrate faster. there was some garbling in the auto-transcript there — prefix/KV cache, the cache management.
[02:15] Asha Menon: security is a big one for our enterprise customers. SOC 2, SSO/SAML, audit logs — can you run through what Redwood exposes for audit and key management?
[02:24] Liam O'Connell: sure — we have audit logs per request with token-level metadata in the Console, SSO via SAML/Okta is supported, and for key management we support customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations for Private deployments. for Hosted we offer encrypted-at-rest with our keys, or customer keys via KMS for Dedicated.
[02:40] David Kim: does Redwood's control plane ever see plaintext customer prompt data in Private?
[02:44] Priya Nair: for Private VPC deployments, the control plane can be customer-managed and you can configure it such that logs are stored in your account; we can minimize telemetry and use cryptographic envelopes to avoid seeing plaintext. we should follow up with the security pack.
[02:57] [pause, someone muffled a laugh]
[03:00] Roberto Silva: ok — thanks. another thing — pricing. if LynxPath resells a Dedicated pool, how do margins look? do you have MSP-friendly SKUs?
[03:10] Ethan Patel: yes we have reserved capacity tiers and a reseller program. i'll include a reseller pricing matrix with example margins and suggested uplift. typical models: per-token usage for hosted, committed monthly for Dedicated, and license + support for Private.
[03:26] Maya Ortiz: and billing – we need a mechanism to white-label invoices or integrate into our billing system.
[03:30] Ethan Patel: yes we support white-label or billing via partner-managed flows; need to dig into legal on the contract but it's a supported pattern.
[03:37] David Kim: networking — latency is a big deal for our EMEA customers. does Redwood offer region pinning and routing policy?
[03:43] Priya Nair: absolutely, Smart routing can pin to region and fallback to compatible model variants in another region if capacity is constrained; region-aware routing and per-route SLOs are part of the Dedicated product.
[03:55] Roberto Silva: for the bench test we want to run a 1k-user chat scenario and measure p95 latency with quantized 13B model. what do you need from us?
[04:03] Priya Nair: ideally: (1) model artifact or name, (2) sample prompts and typical session lengths, (3) RPS profile, (4) network diagram + available GPU types (A100/MI250 etc). we'll run both Dedicated and Private permutations and measure latency and cost per-token.
[04:18] David Kim: we can provide model as 'llama-13b-q8' variant and a dataset of 500 session traces — i'll drop those to you.
[04:25] Asha Menon: on SSO and RBAC — can partners manage their own user roles or does Redwood enforce a single RBAC system?
[04:31] Liam O'Connell: partners can map SAML groups to Redwood roles and manage their users; for Private you can keep identity in your IDP. for hosted flows we support delegated SSO and role mapping.
[04:42] [interruption — faint doorbell, laughter]
[04:46] Roberto Silva: haha — domestic life.
[04:48] Ethan Patel: ok, two quick product notes — (1) Optimize tooling can suggest batch sizes and quantization profiles based on your sample workload; we'll run that on the bench. (2) We have an autoscaling + burst policy so if the pilot needs short bursts for big jobs we can accommodate.
[05:03] Priya Nair: also note — if you want gateway integration with your scheduler, we typically use a lightweight adaptor that talks to Redwood runtime API and performs routing decisions; we can open-source a reference adaptor for your engineer to test.
[05:16] David Kim: that sounds useful, our scheduler is in Go and uses gRPC internally, any SDKs?
[05:21] Priya Nair: we have SDKs in Go/Python/Node and a gRPC shim; the adaptor is basically a small service — we can share code.
[05:29] Roberto Silva: what about compliance artifacts? we need a SOC 2 attestation and backup retention details.
[05:34] Ethan Patel: i'll attach our compliance pack — SOC 2 Type II, ISO intent docs, and the data retention matrix. for Private deployments most customers keep logs on their side which simplifies attestation.
[05:45] Maya Ortiz: procurement — rough timeline for a pilot and then expansion?
[05:49] Ethan Patel: pilot -> bench test week of Jan 12, pilot contract signed by end of Jan (if all good), production pilot Feb-March, expansion in Q2. that aligns with typical procurement windows.
[06:00] Asha Menon: can we get a short slide deck that shows the reseller flow and a sample contract clause for white-label billing?
[06:06] Ethan Patel: yep we'll add that to the next email.
[06:09] [longer pause while someone shares a doc link, transcript picks up words incorrectly: "link to runbook docx" becomes "link to run book docks"]
[06:20] Priya Nair: last bit — instrumentation. we emit traces to the Console and can push traces to your Jaeger/newrelic via OTLP, and we show token-level cost breakdown by route so you can bill customers accurately.
[06:33] David Kim: perfect.
[06:35] Roberto Silva: any gotchas we're not thinking about? like licensing restrictions for open models, or model weights residency rules?
[06:42] Priya Nair: good point — some model licenses restrict commercial hosting, we have a catalog of verified models and can recommend compliant variants; for strict residency we can run fully on-prem with Private + air-gapped patterns but that adds ops overhead.
[06:56] Ethan Patel: ok i think that's a solid set. quick recap — next steps are bench test scheduling, Redwood to send pricing + reseller matrix, security pack, and adaptor reference. LynxPath to provide cluster specs, sample workload, and procurement timelines.
[07:12] Roberto Silva: agreed. thanks all, excited to try this.
[07:15] Maya Ortiz: thanks. we'll follow up on dates.
[07:17] Ethan Patel: thanks everyone, we'll circulate notes and the attachments by EOD.
